source_text: Καὶ γὰρ τὸ εἰρημένον ἐν τῷ νόμῳ, ὅτι Ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὁ κρεμάμενος ἐπὶ ξύλου , οὐχ ὡς τοῦ θεοῦ καταρωμένου τούτου τοῦ ἐσταυρωμένου, ἡμῶν τονοῖ τὴν ἐλπίδα ἐκκρεμαμένην ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυρωθέντος Χριστοῦ, ἀλλ᾿ ὡς προειπόντος τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ ὑφ᾿ ὑμῶν πάντων καὶ τῶν ὁμοίων ὑμῖν, μὴ ἐπισταμένων τοῦτον εἶναι τὸν πρὸ πάντων ὄντα καὶ αἰώνιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἱερέα καὶ βασιλέα καὶ Χριστόν μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι. Ὅπερ καὶ ὄψει ἰδεῖν ὑμῖν ἔστι γινόμενον· ὑμεῖς γὰρ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ὑμῶν καταρᾶσθε πάντων τῶν ἀπ᾿ ἐκεῖνου γενομένων Χριστιανῶν, καὶ τὰ ἄλλα ἔθην, ἃ καὶ ἐνεργῆ τὴν κατάραν ἐργάζονται, ἀναιροῦντα τοὺς μόνον ὁμολογοῦντας ἑαυτοὺς εἶναι Χριστιανούς· οἷς ἡμεῖς ἅπασι λέγομεν, ὅτι Ἀδελφοὶ ἡμῶν ἐστε, ἐπίγνωτε μᾶλλον τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ θεοῦ. Καὶ μὴ πειθομένων ἡμῖν μήτε ἐκείνων μήτε ὑμῶν, ἀλλὰ ἀρνεῖσθαι ἡμᾶς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀγωνιζομένων, θανατοῦσθαι μᾶλλον αἱρούμεθα καὶ ὑπομένομεν, πεπεισμένοι ὅτι πανθ᾿ ὅσα ὑπέσχηται ὁ θεὸς διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀγαθὰ ἀποδώσει ἡμῖν. Καὶ πρὸς τούτοις πᾶσιν εὐχόμεθα ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν, ἵνα ἐλεηθῆτε ὑπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Οὗτος γὰρ ἐδίδαξεν ἡμᾶς καὶ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἐχθρῶν εὔχεσθαι, εἰπών· Γίνεσθε χρηστοὶ καὶ οἰκτίρμονες, ὡς καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος . Καὶ γὰρ τὸν παντοκράτορα θεὸν χρηστὸν καὶ οἰκτίρμονα ὁρῶμεν. τὸν ἥλιον αὐτοῦ ἀνατέλλοντα ἐπὶ ἀχαρίστους καὶ δικαίους, καὶ βρέχοντα ἐπὶ ὁσίους καὶ πονηρούς , οὓς πάντας ὅτι καὶ κρίνειν μέλλει ἐδίδαξε.
pass_a_gloss: For also the thing having been said in the law, that Cursed is every one hanging on a tree, not as God having cursed this one having been crucified, but as God having foretold the things under all of you and those like you, not knowing this one to be the one existing before all and the eternal priest and king and Christ going to become; which also is going to be seen by you; for you in your synagogues curse all the Christians having become from that time, and the other customs, which also work the curse effectively, destroying the ones alone confessing themselves to be Christians; to whom we say all, that You are our brothers, know the truth of God more; and not being persuaded by us, neither by those nor by you, but denying the name of Christ, we choose rather to be killed and endure, having been convinced that all the things which God has promised through Christ, He will give to us as good things; and in addition to all these things, we pray for you, that you may be pitied by Christ; for He taught us also to pray for our enemies, having said: Become kind and merciful, as also your heavenly Father; and for we see the all-powerful God as kind and merciful, His sun rising on ungrateful and righteous, and raining on holy and evil, whom all He also taught that He is going to judge.

bible_refs.note: Cursed is every one hanging on a tree
Become kind and merciful, as also your heavenly Father
His sun rising on ungrateful and righteous, and raining on holy and evil

pass_b_english: The statement in the law that "cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree" (Deuteronomy 21:23) does not mean that God cursed this crucified man; rather, it means that God foretold what you and those like you would do because you do not recognize him as the eternal priest, king, and Christ who existed before all things and was going to appear. You yourselves will see this fulfilled, for in your synagogues you curse all who have become Christians since his time, and other nations effectively carry out that curse by killing those who confess the name of Christ alone. To all of them we say, "You are our brothers; come to know the truth of God more fully." Since neither they nor you are persuaded by us, but instead deny the name of Christ while we strive for it, we choose to die and endure rather than deny him, convinced that God will grant us every good thing he promised through Christ. In addition to all this, we pray for you that Christ may have mercy on you, because he taught us to pray for our enemies, saying, "Be kind and merciful, as your heavenly Father is kind and merciful" (Matthew 5:48). We see that the Almighty God is indeed kind and merciful: he makes his sun rise on the ungrateful and the righteous alike, and sends rain on the holy and the evil (Matthew 5:45) — all of whom he also taught will face his judgment.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the distinction between God cursing the crucified one versus foretelling the rejection of the eternal priest/king. Scripture citations (Deuteronomy 21:23, Matthew 5:48, Matthew 5:45) are correctly identified and applied to the relevant clauses. Pass B correctly interprets the agency and modality of the Greek.
